newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan market slightly lower in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan market slightly lower in thin trade.

text.p: Jordanian shares shed some gains at the start of weekly business on Saturday in quiet trade buttressed by local floor investors buying speculative stock, brokers said.
The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.08 percent to 152.43 points, with buying activity in a handful of speculative and blue-chip stock preventing further declines.
Dealers say recent falls have made some blue chip stock attractively priced, drawing some local investors back into the market in bargain hunting.
"The market was quiet with some rises in mostly speculative stock which are the focus of floor trader activity," said financial analyst Mohammad Abdullah of Pearl Investment.
Turnover was a thin 307,007 dinars ($433,625) with investor focus on select high performing firms.
Political uncertainty combined with a lack of liquidity has recently depressed sentiment and prompted outside buyers and institutional investors to remain on the sidelines.

Among the handful of busy stock were Arab Pharmacuetical Manufacturing which rose 0.01 dinars to 3.65 dinars and Jordan Selpho Chemicals which rose 0.03 dinars to 0.75 dinars. Jordan Electric Power rose 0.01 dinars to 1.66 in the second busiest trade of the day worth 34,182 dinars.
The market on Saturday saw 14 shares rising while a similar number fell. Another 13 were traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.07 percent to 80.10 points, 3.95 percent down from the start of the year.
